title: Thousands march in Madrid following the death of an evicted 87-year-old woman
seoTitle: Madrid housing protest over eviction death

tea.why: Protesters marched to express anger over Spain's housing crisis following the death of an 87-year-old woman evicted from her home.
tea.want: Protesters and unions are demanding action on housing issues, with trade unions announcing a nationwide general strike.
tea.changed: Oct 7: Thousands marched from Puerta del Sol to parliament after the death of an evicted woman, and unions announced a general strike.

summary: Thousands of demonstrators marched in Madrid from the Puerta del Sol square towards parliament, chanting slogans after the death of an 87-year-old woman who had been hospitalized following her eviction last month. Organised and reported by the Madrid tenants' union, the protest highlighted widespread anger over Spain's severe housing shortage and rising rents. The eviction and subsequent protests have heavily impacted national politics, leading Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call an early election for November 29 after parliament rejected decrees aimed at curbing evictions and rent pressures. Trade unions also announced a nationwide general strike over housing for November 11. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressed condolences on social media, while opposition People's Party leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo stated that the death should not be politicized.
demands: Measures to curb evictions and limit rent pressures
